it.name: Italy

law.label: Law 91/1992, art. 3-bis (added by Decree-Law 36/2025, converted by Law 74/2025)

it.authority: the Italian consulate for your US address (from 1 January 2029, a central office of the Foreign Ministry in Rome)

fee.label: Consular fee for recognition, per adult

usdFee.label: Same fee in dollars at the New York consulate, October 1 to December 31, 2026

time.text: 730 days legal limit (24 months at San Francisco); 36 months for adult files under Law 11/2026

dual.text: No renunciation of US citizenship (art. 11 of Law 91/1992).

it.gens: Parent or grandparent only, since March 28, 2025

ie.name: Ireland

law.label: Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 1956, s. 7 (as amended)

ie.authority: the Department of Foreign Affairs (Foreign Births Register, online)

fee.label: Foreign Birth Registration, applicant 18 or over (EUR 270 + EUR 8 postage)

time.text: about 12 months for a complete application, in strict date order

ie.gens: Parent born in Ireland (automatic) or grandparent born in Ireland (register)

gb.name: United Kingdom
gb.authority: UK Visas and Immigration (online forms UKM, UKF, MN1)

fee.label: Registration under s. 4C (form UKM) or as child of an unmarried father (UKF): citizenship ceremony fee only

feeChild.label: Registering a child under s. 3(2) (form MN1)

feeStatus.label: Confirmation that you are already British (form NS)

time.text: usually within 6 months (about 30 working days with priority)

dual.text: Dual citizenship is allowed in the UK.

gb.gens: One generation born abroad (a parent born in the UK)

pl.name: Poland

law.label: Polish Citizenship Act of 2 April 2009, with the 1920 and 1951 Acts for earlier births

pl.authority: a Polish consulate in the US, which forwards the file to a voivode (regional governor) in Poland

fee.label: Consular fee for filing a confirmation application in the US

feePoland.label: Stamp duty when filed directly with the voivode (Łódź office)

time.text: no decision time published by the voivodes

dual.text: Tolerated: Poland treats a dual citizen solely as Polish on its territory.

pl.gens: No limit, if every link was still Polish when the next child was born

ca.name: Canada

law.label: Citizenship Act, s. 3, as amended by Bill C-3 (S.C. 2025, c. 5)

ca.authority: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (proof of citizenship certificate)

time.text: not published for certificates on the pages read; a citizenship record search is shown at 19 months (October 21, 2026)

dual.text: Canada allows multiple citizenship; you need a Canadian passport to fly back to Canada.

ca.gens: No limit for people born before December 15, 2025; after that, 1,095 days of the parent's presence in Canada

no.name: Norway

law.label: Norwegian Nationality Act 2005, ss. 4, 22 a and 24

no.authority: the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI), through a Norwegian mission in the US

fee.label: Getting Norwegian citizenship back by notification, adult

time.text: 3 months for former citizens' notifications (updated September 24, 2026)

no.gens: Parent only, Norwegian when you were born

de.name: Germany

law.label: Nationality Act (StAG) ss. 4, 5 and 15; Basic Law art. 116(2)

de.authority: the Federal Office of Administration (BVA) in Cologne, through a German mission in the US

fee.label: Certificate of citizenship for people already German by descent

feeS15.label: Naturalisation under s. 15 StAG or art. 116(2) (free)

time.text: two to three years for a certificate of citizenship; no time published for s. 5, s. 15 or art. 116(2)

dual.text: Accepted generally since June 27, 2024; losses before that date stay.

de.gens: No limit, if every link was still German when the next child was born

at.name: Austria

law.label: Nationality Act 1985 (StbG), s. 58c, and s. 7 for descent at birth

at.authority: the Vienna provincial government (MA 35), through the Austrian embassy or consulate for your US address

time.text: not published; MA 35 closed 10,420 s. 58c files in 2025

dual.text: No renunciation for s. 58c, but acquiring another citizenship after filing costs Austrian citizenship retroactively; outside s. 58c Austria generally forbids dual citizenship.

at.gens: Parent only at birth; no limit for descendants of persecuted people (s. 58c)

fr.name: France
fr.authority: the nationality service of the Paris judicial court (certificate of French nationality)

time.text: 6 months from the receipt, extendable twice by 6 months (18 months at most)

dual.text: No renunciation of US citizenship; French nationals who take another nationality keep French nationality unless they declare otherwise.

fr.gens: No limit in law, but blocked after 50 years abroad without French papers (art. 30-3)

se.name: Sweden

law.label: Swedish Citizenship Act (2001:82), as amended from June 6, 2026

se.authority: the Swedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket), through a Swedish embassy or consulate

feeFather.label: Notification by a Swedish father, child born abroad out of wedlock before April 1, 2015

time.text: 7 months for a father's notification; not published for declarations

se.gens: Parent only, Swedish when you were born

es.name: Spain

law.label: Civil Code, arts. 17 to 26; Democratic Memory Law 20/2022 (window closed October 22, 2025)

es.authority: the civil registry of the Spanish consulate for your US address

fee.label: Civil registry procedures: option, recovery, registration (free)

time.text: around 6 to 8 weeks for registration after an option at the New York consulate

dual.text: An option under art. 20 requires a declaration renouncing US nationality before Spanish authorities; Spaniards by origin keep both.

es.gens: Parent born in Spain (option at any age); grandchildren only through the Democratic Memory Law, closed on October 22, 2025

pt.name: Portugal

law.label: Nationality Law 37/81, art. 1(1)(c) and (d), as amended by Organic Law 1/2026

pt.authority: the Central Registry Office (IRN) in Lisbon, through the Portuguese consulate for your US address

fee.label: Registry fee: not stated on the official guide pages read

time.text: no average time published by the registry

dual.text: No renunciation required; Portuguese nationality ends only by a declaration of the person.

pt.gens: Parent, or grandparent with a language and culture test since May 19, 2026

mx.name: Mexico

law.label: Constitution, art. 30 A(II), as amended on May 17, 2021

mx.authority: the civil registry of the Mexican consulate for your US address

fee.label: Birth registration for dual nationality, one certified copy included (Atlanta consulate)

time.text: no time published; the record is made at the appointment

dual.text: A Mexican by birth cannot lose Mexican nationality; you enter and leave Mexico as a Mexican.

mx.gens: No limit since May 18, 2021: each generation registers in turn

gr.name: Greece
gr.authority: the Greek consulate for your US address, which registers you in a municipal register in Greece

fee.label: Registration of a person Greek from birth: no fee in the Code

feeArt26.label: Determination of citizenship under art. 26, or naturalization of a person of Greek origin

dual.text: Taking another citizenship does not end Greek citizenship without the Interior Minister's permission.

gr.gens: No limit, generation by generation, each one registered in Greece

hu.name: Hungary

law.label: Act LV of 1993 on Hungarian Citizenship, s. 4(3)

hu.authority: the Hungarian consulate for your US address (citizenship verification or simplified naturalization)

time.text: several months for a verification (New York consulate); 3 months, extendable by 3, for the minister's step of a naturalization

dual.text: Hungary does not ask you to give up US citizenship.

hu.gens: No limit for simplified naturalization, with a conversation in Hungarian

cz.name: Czech Republic

law.label: Act 186/2013 on Czech Citizenship, s. 31 (as amended by Act 207/2019)

cz.authority: a Czech consulate in the US, which forwards the declaration to the regional office

fee.label: Declaration of acquisition (s. 31) at a Czech consulate in the US

usdFee.label: Same fee in dollars, October 2026 consular schedule

time.text: the consulate forwards the declaration within 30 days; no decision time published

dual.text: Since January 1, 2014 Czech citizens keep their citizenship when they take another.

cz.gens: Children and grandchildren of a former citizen (declaration)

sk.name: Slovakia
sk.authority: the Ministry of the Interior, through a Slovak embassy or consulate

fee.label: Grant to a person with a Czechoslovak parent, grandparent or great-grandparent born in Slovakia

time.text: 24 months at most from receipt by the Ministry

dual.text: No renunciation of US citizenship is asked, but a Slovak citizen who later naturalizes abroad loses it, save exceptions.

sk.gens: Parent, grandparent or great-grandparent born in Slovakia (discretionary grant)
